definitions.explanation: A piece cut out of a newspaper or magazine, typically an article, photograph, or recipe, saved for reference or collection.

definitions.gloss: a short clip or highlight (from video or audio)
definitions.explanation: A short segment extracted from a longer video or audio recording, such as a highlight reel or a fan-made excerpt from a livestream, widely shared on social media.

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きを{集|あつ}めている。
{母|はは}は{料理|りょうり}のレシピの{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きをノートに{貼|は}っている。
examples.english: My mother pastes recipe clippings into a notebook.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{雑誌|ざっし}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きが{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しから{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: Old magazine clippings came out of the drawer.

examples.japanese: その{動画|どうが}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きがSNSで{話題|わだい}になった。
examples.english: A clip from that video became a topic on social media.

examples.japanese: {配信|はいしん}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きをYouTubeに{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: I uploaded a clip from the livestream to YouTube.

examples.japanese: {面白|おもしろ}い{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きを{友達|ともだち}に{送|おく}った。
examples.english: I sent a funny clip to a friend.

notes:
Derived from the verb {切|き}り{抜|ぬ}く (to cut out). Traditionally refers to newspaper or magazine clippings physically cut from print media. In modern usage, especially online, it refers to short video clips extracted from longer content such as livestreams or podcasts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新聞|しんぶん}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}き: newspaper clipping
- {記事|きじ}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}き: article clipping
- {動画|どうが}の{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}き: video clip
- {切|き}り{抜|ぬ}きを{集|あつ}める: to collect clippings

CULTURAL NOTE:
In online culture, {切|き}り{抜|ぬ}き videos (short highlight clips from longer livestreams) have become extremely popular on platforms like YouTube, often made by fans of streamers and content creators.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スクラップ: scrapbook clipping — specifically for pasting into a scrapbook
- {抜粋|ばっすい}: excerpt — more formal, usually refers to text excerpts
